name: MATH
summary: 5,000 competition-mathematics test problems across seven subjects and five difficulty levels, each with a worked reference solution.
overview: MATH tests whether a model can solve competition mathematics problems and produce a final answer. The test set has 5,000 problems in algebra, counting and probability, geometry, intermediate algebra, number theory, prealgebra, and precalculus. Problems are marked from difficulty level 1 through level 5, and each one has a worked solution. The benchmark was introduced in March 2021 and published at NeurIPS 2021. [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03874)
methodology:
This snapshot contains all 5,000 records in the test split: algebra (1,187), counting and probability (474), geometry (479), intermediate algebra (903), number theory (540), prealgebra (871), and precalculus (546). It excludes the 7,500 training problems and the separate AMPS pretraining set. Counts are taken from the pinned dataset card. [Dataset card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/EleutherAI/hendrycks_math/blob/21a5633873b6a120296cce3e2df9d5550074f4a3/README.md)

The problems are not stored in the authors' git repository. An earlier README links to an author-hosted archive that returned no file when this snapshot was imported. The current README links to a third-party copy that merges the problems into one split. This snapshot instead uses the EleutherAI/hendrycks_math mirror at the pinned revision, which keeps one test file per subject. [Authors' repository](https://github.com/hendrycks/math/blob/985bdc1696e88e8643f081a0ff4719da39f2ae2a/README.md)

Each Task Prompt preserves the upstream problem verbatim. The Solution preserves the upstream worked solution verbatim, including the final answer inside a boxed expression. The importer checks that every row has a difficulty from level 1 through level 5 and the subject label that belongs to its file. The subject is part of the task ID. The difficulty label is not stored on the task. The source has no problem IDs. IDs are the subject plus test-0001 upward, assigned by one-based row order in that subject's pinned test file. Prompt and solution source links open that row in the dataset viewer, which follows the current dataset revision. [Dataset card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/EleutherAI/hendrycks_math/blob/21a5633873b6a120296cce3e2df9d5550074f4a3/README.md)

These pages show individual problems. They do not add the few-shot examples used by the original evaluation script. No task-specific software environment is required to read them. Some problems include a figure as Asymptote drawing code inside the problem text. The importer reads the pinned Parquet files with PyArrow and can be rerun with python3 data/math/import.py.
scoring:
A problem is correct when the model's final answer matches the reference final answer. The authors' evaluation script takes the last boxed expression in the worked solution, removes the box markup, and compares that string with the model answer. The comparison normalizes surface differences such as whitespace, fraction formatting, square roots, and units, then requires the remaining strings to be equal. A model answer with no comparable final answer is incorrect. The script reports the fraction correct for each subject, each difficulty level, and the full test set. [Evaluation script](https://github.com/hendrycks/math/blob/985bdc1696e88e8643f081a0ff4719da39f2ae2a/modeling/evaluate_gpt3.py) and [answer comparison](https://github.com/hendrycks/math/blob/985bdc1696e88e8643f081a0ff4719da39f2ae2a/modeling/math_equivalence.py)

Compare results that use the same prompting, sampling, and answer extraction. Benchopedia's sweep asks for a boxed final answer and grades it with the authors' extraction and equivalence functions. The published worked solutions remain in the snapshot. [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03874)
limitations:
These tasks are English high-school contest problems, so a score does not by itself establish research-level mathematics or general reasoning. Matching the final answer does not establish that every written step is correct. Figures are stored as Asymptote source inside the problem text, and these pages do not draw them. Difficulty labels are checked at import and are not shown on the task page. [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03874) and [evaluation script](https://github.com/hendrycks/math/blob/985bdc1696e88e8643f081a0ff4719da39f2ae2a/modeling/evaluate_gpt3.py)

The displayed problem alone does not reproduce a complete model evaluation: few-shot examples and answer extraction can change results. The 5,000 imported problem texts are distinct. The imported text is preserved as published rather than independently corrected. This is the original 5,000-problem test split, not a smaller subset. The problems and answers are public, so a score alone cannot establish that a model was tested on unseen material.
